subject: Post-call recap & load test coordination — Finwise (k6/streaming SLOs)
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Samir Shah <samir@finwise.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap & load test coordination — Finwise (k6/streaming SLOs)

Thanks Samir — great sync earlier. Quick recap + next steps to keep us aligned on the Finwise performance qualification and the customer-led load test: 

TL;DR: Redwood can support your latency & streaming SLOs; next is a customer-led k6 run next Wednesday (4/28) during the 9-11am PT window. We will provide a test account, an example k6 script, IP ranges to allowlist, and a short runbook.

Recap from the call:
- Target SLOs: 95th percentile latency <= 350ms for single-turn generation (prompt length ~60 tokens), and 99th percentile streaming frame latency <= 150ms when using streaming (server->client chunking).
- Throughput/concurrency: target steady throughput of 120 requests/s with bursts to 250 rps for up to 10 minutes; concurrency would be ~60 concurrent sessions (streaming).
- Streaming requirements: chunk size ~800-1200 bytes, client expects initial frame within 80-100ms after request acceptance.
- Test harness: you'll run k6 (customer-led) against our staging endpoint; we'll provide a test API key and a small sample k6 script that exercises both non-stream and streaming paths.

Action items (owners):
1) Redwood (Logan/Marissa): create test account + API key, upload k6 sample script, share IP allowlist and runbook (by EOD Friday 4/23).
2) Finwise (Samir/Olivia): confirm the test window (prefer Wed 4/28 9-11am PT) and provide any CIDR ranges or proxy IPs we should expect the traffic from.
3) Joint: brief smoke run on staging (10m) the day before to confirm auth & routing.

Attachments: finwise_k6_script_v1.js (k6 script stub), redwood_test_account_instructions.md (runbook).

If that looks right, Samir — can you confirm the window and share the external IP list you'll use?

Thanks,
Logan
Account Executive
Redwood Inference

--
Logan Wright | logan.wright@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0124

From: Samir Shah <samir@finwise.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Olivia Turner <olivia.turner@finwise.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & load test coordination — Finwise (k6/streaming SLOs)

Thanks Logan — that recap matches our notes. Wed 4/28 9-11am PT works for us.

A couple quick asks from our infra/security side before the run: 
- IP allowlist: we will be running the k6 load from our cloud provider (Finwise test account) and through a NAT. Current source IP ranges will be: 52.23.112.0/24 and 52.23.113.0/24. If you need specific egress IPs, we can lock that down and confirm by EOD Monday.
- Test accounts: please confirm the test API key will be scoped to non-production data and revoked after testing. We will need a doc with the endpoint, auth header example, and usage limits (rps).
- Script questions: does the sample k6 script include streaming tokenization and chunk consumption (we want to simulate a client that processes streaming frames)?

For the SLOs — the 95p 350ms for single-turn is our goal; the streaming frame latencies are more important for UX, so we'll be watching 99p closely. We'll do a longer soak (2-3 hours) next quarter if this short test looks good.

Samir
Director of Engineering, Finwise
samir@finwise.com

--

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 17:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & load test coordination — Finwise (k6/streaming SLOs)

Samir — thanks, and those IP ranges look good as a starting point. A few confirmations and updates from our side: 

1) Test account + API key: created and scoped to a staging dataset; key: TEST-FIN-20270428-XXXX (we'll send the actual key via the runbook doc link below). Key will be revoked after testing unless you request extension for a scheduled soak.
2) k6 script: attached as finwise_k6_script_v1.js. It includes both a non-streaming path (POST /v1/generate) and a streaming path that uses a websocket-like chunk consumer (k6 can't fully replicate browser streaming, but the script uses small chunk pulls to approximate client consumption). See comments in the script for where to adjust chunk intervals and payload sizes.
3) IP allowlist: please add the 52.23.112.0/24 and 52.23.113.0/24 ranges to your firewall rules; we will also allow 34.82.201.10/32 and 34.82.201.11/32 (Redwood staging egress) in case any calls route via our test proxies.
4) Runbook & limits: redwood_test_account_instructions.md (attached) contains endpoint, header example, rate limits, and a step-by-step smoke checklist. Rate limits for the staging key are set to 350 rps per project with a per-connection soft concurrency cap of 200 - the script will ramp to your target of 120 rps and can burst to 250.

Proposed schedule:
- Mon 4/26: smoke run (10m) by Finwise to validate auth + routing (we can be on the call at 9:30am PT).
- Wed 4/28 09:00-11:00 PT: full customer-led load test (k6). Redwood will monitor and provide a live dashboard link and latency/streaming frame charts.

Please confirm the Monday smoke run and let us know if you will lock down the exact egress IPs.

Thanks,
Logan

Attachments:
- finwise_k6_script_v1.js (attachment)
- redwood_test_account_instructions.md (attachment)
